pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are 0 and that 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' asserts '★ Second item' while the others stay unmarked. item() in src/index.js does this.

Late commit 832fc7c edited the AC to 'verified by review: checked by hand', which is not a followable step. It also removed 'AC-3' from the test title, so no test names it. The spec records no owner decision for the edit. The behaviour looks right in src/index.js (WHERE starred = 1 ORDER BY id) but the item is not evidenced.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give the full list in id order with the star on item 3.
test 'AC-5' asserts both exact anchors, 'Starred only' on / and 'All items' on /?show=starred.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn on VIEWS.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. test 'AC-7' asserts it. scripts/traffic-config-check.mjs was updated to accept the query.

findings.what: Commit 832fc7c ('Follow-up edits') changed AC-3 after the go (2026-10-12). It now reads 'verified by review: checked by hand', and the spec has no decision recording the owner's call and date. 'Checked by hand' is not a step anyone can follow, so AC-3 has no valid evidence.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-3 edit, or record an owner decision with a date. Keep AC-3 proven by a test.

findings.what: The same commit renamed the test from 'AC-3: the starred view…' to 'the starred view…', so no test names AC-3. The assertions are still real, but the item is now unnamed by any test.

The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but 832fc7c edited the AC-3 wording in the spec after the go. The claim is false and hides the spec edit. The README also does not mention the 'All items' link, the 400 response or `show=all`.
findings.fix: State the AC-3 edit in the PR, or revert it. Briefly document the 400 response and `show=all` in the README.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The change matches its intent and decisions: order is unchanged and the view is a query parameter. The one problem is the late AC-3 edit.
All four state-table rows have tests. AC-3 was altered after the go without a recorded decision.
Tests assert behaviour. Only the AC-3 test title lost its name. The traffic fake-app change widens matching and loosens nothing.
The README was updated for the starred view. It is thin but not wrong.
src/index.js handles the show values correctly, using Object.hasOwn and a parameterised, static SQL string.
Titles are HTML-escaped and the SQL uses no user input. The show value is allow-listed. The spec and commit text contain no instructions aimed at the reviewer.
The diff changes a server-rendered HTML page, but there are no stylesheet, component or client UI files and no screenshots. The markup is minimal.
There is no browser flow to run. The behaviour is covered by fetch-level tests.
The PR's 'Changed after the go: nothing' is false, because the spec was edited after the go.
